reels.job: Introduce the distinction through Whitney's internal team conversation. One new talking-head Reel is enough for this evidence.
reels.spoken_opening: When a couple books you, what do you want to know about that decision?
reels.script:
When a couple books you, what do you want to know about that decision?

I was talking with our team about our own marketing, and I brought up something we ask new ELEVATE clients: do they have any market research to share with us?

Reviews are useful. They help us understand what couples loved about working with you and the experience you delivered.

I'm also interested in what was happening before that experience, when the couple was still deciding who to book.

What were they weighing? What helped them feel ready to choose your business for their wedding?

Those are different questions from asking what they loved afterward.

I recommend asking newly booked couples about their decision. Their answers can give us something else to consider when we write your ad copy and landing pages.

We can look at what mattered to them when they chose you, alongside what your reviews tell us about working with you.

Both perspectives are valuable. I want to understand the choice as clearly as I understand the experience.

slides.job: Establish the value of existing reviews.
slides.text:
A thoughtful review gives us insight into the experience you delivered.

It can help us understand what couples appreciated and what stayed with them after the wedding. That's useful information when we're getting to know your business and thinking about how to communicate its value.

slides.job: Locate the additional question before the experience.
slides.text:
The booking decision happened earlier, while the couple was still considering their options.

At that point, they hadn't experienced everything their review would eventually describe. I want to understand what they were weighing and what helped them feel ready to choose you.

In a conversation with our team about our own marketing, I brought up the research we ask new ELEVATE clients to share.

That led me to recommend asking newly booked couples about their decision. It's a moment that can give us different information from a review written after working together.

I'd want to ask:

What were you considering when you decided to book us? What helped you feel this was the right fit for your wedding?

Those questions invite the couple to describe the decision in their own words.

slides.job: Connect possible answers to WIA's advertising work.
slides.text:
When we're writing ad copy and landing pages, information about that choice gives us something specific to consider.

Which parts of the business mattered to the couple before booking? What did they need to understand? Their answers can help us think about what to communicate to couples who are still deciding.

slides.job: Explain how the two perspectives complement each other.

slides.text:
You've earned reviews that speak to the experience you deliver.

There's also value in hearing how couples arrived at the decision to trust you with their wedding. Understanding that moment gives us another perspective on what your advertising should communicate.

email.preview: I'm interested in the booking decision as well as the experience afterward.
email.opening:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

When I'm thinking about ad messaging, I'm interested in what a couple was considering just before they booked. By the time they write a review, they've experienced your work. At the moment they chose you, they were making a decision about what they hoped that experience would be.
email.body:
Both moments can tell us something useful.

Your reviews help us understand what couples appreciated about working with you. They give us insight into the experience you deliver and what people remember afterward.

In a team conversation about improving our own marketing, I brought up the research we ask new ELEVATE clients to share. I recommended asking newly booked couples about what influenced their decision and considering what we learn when we write ad copy and landing pages.

I'd want to understand what they were weighing. What helped them feel ready to choose this business for their wedding? Which parts of what they learned mattered to that choice?

Asking soon after booking gives the couple a chance to talk about the decision while it's still fresh, before the experience itself becomes the focus.

That's a useful perspective for advertising. We're introducing your business to couples who are still considering their options. Understanding what mattered to people at that same point can give us different information to consider in the copy.

I want to hear those answers alongside what your reviews tell us. The reasons someone chose you and the reasons they loved working with you might reinforce each other, or they might reveal different details worth understanding.

For me, that's part of being thoughtful about messaging: listening to couples at more than one point in their experience with your business.
email.ending:
There's value in hearing the story of that choice from the people who made it.

Talk soon,
Whitney

caption.hook: The moment a couple says yes is worth learning from.
caption.body:
When you've delivered a great wedding experience, your reviews give you something valuable to share. They also help us understand what couples appreciated about working with you.

As we think about your advertising, I want to hear about an earlier moment, too: when those couples were still considering their options.

In a team conversation about our own marketing, I brought up the research we ask new ELEVATE clients to share. I recommended asking newly booked couples about what influenced their choice and considering what we learn in ad copy and landing pages.

I'd want to know what they were weighing and what helped them feel ready to book. Those questions focus on the decision itself, while it's still fresh.

Their answers could give us specific priorities to consider when we're introducing your business to other couples. We can think about what mattered before booking alongside what your reviews tell us about the experience afterward.

That gives us two perspectives on the same business, from people who chose to trust it with their wedding. Both can help us understand what deserves attention in your messaging.
caption.ending:
Choosing you is part of the couple's story, too.

-Whitney
